page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.8xlarge is a big data and dense-storage instance within the ecs.d1 family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. It provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Networking throughput features a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps. The configuration does not include GPU accelerators.

A core characteristic of ecs.d1.8xlarge is its bundled high-capacity local storage subsystem, which delivers 94489 GB across spinning hard disk drives (HDD). This massive raw capacity is paired with sequential read and write operations common to dense magnetic disks. While HDD media exhibits higher seek latency and lower random IOPS compared to solid-state or NVMe drives, the massive volume density provides significant cost efficiency for large data footprints where high random I/O rates are not strictly required.

Because of its balance of 32 compute cores, moderate memory capacity, 10 Gbps network bandwidth, and near-95 TB of local disk storage, ecs.d1.8xlarge is positioned for distributed big data processing, data warehousing, log aggregation, and batch analytics platforms such as Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark, and large-scale ETL pipelines that process massive datasets sequentially.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.8xlarge is a dedicated big data instance within the ecs.d1 series, operating on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM, yielding a 4 GB per core ratio. Its primary differentiator is an integrated 94489 GB local HDD array, accompanied by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include GPU acceleration. The deployment of spinning hard disks maximizes storage volume per instance, offering an economical resource profile for immense datasets where sequential I/O dominates over random access. Consequently, ecs.d1.8xlarge is tailored for data-intensive architectures, including distributed file systems, Hadoop clusters, large-scale batch processing, log archiving, and data ingestion pipelines.
